verdict.rationale: Abacum's own docs describe assumption-driven planning: assumptions are connected to forecasts and scenarios so the plan updates without rebuilding (abacum-docs-6), and changing an assumption moves revenue, hiring and cash together (abacum-docs-16). Headcount planning sits in the same connected model (abacum-docs-17), alongside bottom-up inputs (abacum-docs-15) and an AI Modeler that needs no formulas (abacum-docs-1). That covers the hiring driver and the general assumptions-over-hard-coded-rows idea, but the specific growth and price-point drivers are never shown. All evidence is vendor marketing. Missing for 10: explicit documentation of driver-based modeling, growth-rate and price-point (price × volume) drivers, docs on how drivers are defined and linked, and independent or hands-on confirmation.
